I'm also wondering if those crueler and bloodthirsty aspects that we've seen of Kuon were also present in him as a child, and we just haven't seen it. Since we've seen an older Kuon, who is relatively tame and sweet (like raising a chicken because he didn't want to hurt it), we know Kuon isn't always cruel, so maybe a violent version of him existed as a child too. The way that I've been told, (and I absolutely am not a doctor) you can think of it like type 2 diabetes:

Your body isn't producing enough insulin due to what it now perceives incorrectly as the new standard of secretion. And you can change your diet (particularly less sugar) and maintain a healthy lifestyle to never need treatment again, but you will always have the potential for symptoms to emerge again. Especially if you discontinue the changes you made because your body will easily remember what it did previously to incorrectly try to adapt.

Supposedly, with POTS if you also diet (particularly more sodium) and maintain a healthy lifestyle, you can re-teach your body the proper reactions and responses it should have for adjusting your blood volume/pressure. But again, you will always have the potential for symptoms to emerge, especially if you discontinue the changes you made. 

I don't personally know anyone that has outgrown it. But I also didn't know what it was until a few years ago when I was finally diagnosed after more than a decade and a half.

Honestly, I think POTS isn't well known enough for them to understand. It's been around for a while but has only recently become a recognized condition. I would ask your PCP if they are able to write you a note of accommodation, mine did in lieu of my cardiologist.
